_note: Tracked cross-unit threads. Hand-authored — this is policy, nothing derives it. A data-root listed here as `root` gets this thread's colour in EVERY unit it appears in (global tier). Roots not listed here fall back to the unit's local palette in units.json. To recolour a thread book-wide, change its `color` here. `opens`/`payoffs` are for the trajectory popover; `status` open|closed. `tagged: false` means the thread is real in the commentary but not yet marked with data-root spans in the fragments — see pipeline/out/retrofit-*.md. COVERAGE POLICY (2026-09-09): a tracked root is tagged `<span class="r" data-root="id">` at EVERY morphological occurrence in a unit, even in units before the thread's `opens`. `opens`/`payoffs` stay the editorial trajectory (what the popover narrates), NOT the first sighting. Audit: pipeline/out/thread-retrofit-audit.md.

payoffs.note: light curdling back to darkness

threads.note: Isa 9 light dawns on the people (4:16) -> 'y'all are the light of the world' (5:14). Watch the light/dark pair across the 4/5 seam.

payoffs.note: the door held shut (10:5, 'no road of the nations') then cracked ajar (10:18, 'a testimony to the nations')
the servant announces judgment to the nations, and in his name nations will hope — a Gentile horizon inside the Sabbath conflicts.

threads.note: 'Galilee of the nations' (4:15) -> 'make disciples of all the nations' (28:19). One leg of the Emmanuel/nations frame around the whole book.

payoffs.note: lands cleanly on 'the disciples' after two failed would-be followers
Matthew rises and follows; the ruler and the two blind men followed
'follow behind me' now paired with taking up a cross — the cost stated

threads.note: Used of the four (4:20, 22) AND of the crowds (4:25); the ambiguity is what 5:1 opens on. A discipleship keyword from Unit 4 on.

payoffs.note: the dragnet parable

threads.note: 'Fishers of men' (4:19) carries OT judgement freight (Jer 16:16; Hab 1; Amos 4; Ezek 29) in tension with gathering-for-restoration.

payoffs.note: the sea as a structural mirror between the storm (8:24-25) and the pigs (8:32)
The sea, stage of chaos and authority since ch. 8, becomes a lectern (13:1–2) and then the water the dragnet sweeps (13:47).
the stage of chaos in 8:24–32 becomes the floor he walks on

threads.note: Sea/Galilee geography in Unit 4; in Unit 8 the sea becomes a chaos-and-authority stage.
Two 'from that time' hinges: 4:17 ('began to proclaim') <-> 16:21 ('began to show he must suffer'). Read the two together at Unit 17.

payoffs.note: 'this is the Law and the Prophets' — inclusio closed
'all the prophets and the law' — the inclusio's own vocabulary returns, order reversed, prophets now first; reopened after being marked closed at 7:12

threads.note: Frames the body of the Sermon, opened 5:17 and closed 7:12. Spanned Units 5-7; now closed.

payoffs.note: applied to the disciples themselves for the first time

threads.note: Matthew's near-nickname for the disciples (oligopistoi). Distinct from the `faith` thread (pistis, the centurion's) — different word, own colour.

payoffs.note: the fever's release points forward to the paralytic's forgiveness
every sin and defaming will be released — except one; the verb of 6:12 and 9:2 meets its limit.
'Let both grow together' — the master releases the urge to purge until the harvest.

threads.note: Same verb for letting go a debt, a fever, a boat, the dead. Unit 6 prayer -> Unit 8 healings -> Unit 9 forgiveness.

payoffs.note: the centurion, a man under authority
the Son of Man has authority on earth to release sins; the crowds see it given to human beings
the exousia is handed to the Twelve — no precedent in Israel's story
'all authority has been given to me'

threads.note: The crowds marvel that he teaches with authority (7:29); it runs to the mountain of commission (28:18).

threads.gloss: throw / cast / put / pour / clothe (broad range)

payoffs.note: the paralytic thrown on his mat, wine poured into skins, the mourners thrown out, demons cast out
God thrusts out workers, the Twelve throw out demons, then Jesus comes to throw not peace but a sword
one verb for the servant who 'throws out' judgment to victory, the demons thrown out, and the good thrown out of a good treasure.
The dragnet 'thrown' into the sea; the rotten 'thrown outside' (13:48); the lawless 'thrown into the furnace' (13:42, 50); the scribe 'throws out' new and old (13:52).

threads.note: Unit 8 cluster: the tormented servant thrown down (8:6), the sons of the kingdom cast out (8:12), the fever, the storm. Watch for the dragnet and the outer darkness later.
The 'great seismos' on the sea (8:24) is the same word as the earthquakes at the cross and the tomb.

payoffs.note: the demons: 'have you come to torment us before the time?'
the boat ‘tormented by the waves’ — the torment word moves onto the sea

threads.note: Inclusio inside Unit 8 — the servant tormented by illness (8:6) and the demons fearing torment (8:29). Watch for eschatological torment later.

payoffs.note: the demons beg, then the whole town begs him to leave
Gennesaret urges him to let them touch; Gadara urged him to leave (8:34)

threads.note: The centurion entreats (8:5), the demons entreat (8:31), the town entreats him to go (8:34) — the same verb bends from faith to rejection.

payoffs.note: authority on earth to release sins — the first payoff of the 8:20 opening
"until the Son of Man comes" — the coming-with-the-clouds sense, interpretively unsettled
the Son of Man claims mastery of the Sabbath (12:8), is spoken against (12:32), and will lie three days in the heart of the earth (12:40).
The sower of good seed is the Son of Man (13:37), who also sends 'his angels' to collect out of 'his kingdom' (13:41).

threads.note: Daniel 7:13-14 — one like a son of man given everlasting dominion. Runs from 8:20 to the trial and the parousia.
First direct address at 9:27, always a cry from the desperate and always tied to healing — the 'therapeutic Son of David' pattern. Runs to the entry and the temple (21:9, 15).

payoffs.note: Hosea 6:6 quoted verbatim again, same critics

threads.note: Hosea 6:6 (eleos = LXX for hesed, covenant loyalty, not mere pity): 'I want loyal-love and not sacrifice.' Cited at 9:13, repeated at 12:7, cried out at 9:27.

payoffs.note: the double sense at full stretch — 'your trust has saved you'
'the one enduring to the end will be saved' — rescue tied to endurance, not a crisis-moment
'he saved others; he cannot save himself'

threads.note: sōzō — 'he will save his people from their sins' (1:21) carries a heal/rescue double sense Matthew never forces apart, running to the irony at the cross.

threads.gloss: sin, failure to hit the mark

payoffs.note: 'your sins are released' (9:2-6), then the table of tax-collectors and sinners he says he came to call (9:10-13, closing on Hosea 6:6)
'a friend of tax collectors and sinners' — the same charge and the same word as the meal at 9:10-13
the cup 'poured out for many for release of sins' — the thread's terminus

threads.note: hamartia / hamartōlos — named at 1:21 as the thing the whole rescue is aimed at ('he will save his people from their sins'), not political liberation. Runs through John's baptism of confession (3:6) to Unit 9, where releasing sins and healing a body are made one act (9:2-6) and the sinners themselves are who Jesus says he came to call (9:10-13), and lands at the cup (26:28). Pairs with save (1:21) and release (aphiēmi, 9:2).

payoffs.note: the sick beg to touch it, and are healed
the scribes lengthen theirs for show — the reversal

threads.note: kraspedon — the tzitzit of Numbers 15:38. Touched in faith and healing at 9:20 and 14:36; worn for display at 23:5.

payoffs.note: 'shrewd as the snakes and unalloyed as the doves' — sent into a hostile world

threads.note: The shrewd builder on rock (7:24); shrewd as snakes for the road (10:16); the faithful and shrewd slave (24:45); the five shrewd virgins (25:2).
The foolish builder on sand (7:26); 'fools and blind' (23:17); the five foolish virgins (25:2).

payoffs.note: 'on this rock I will build my assembly'

threads.note: The wise builder builds on rock (7:24) -> 'I will build my assembly' (16:18).

payoffs.note: 'on this rock' — Petros / petra

threads.note: The house founded on petra (7:24-25) -> Peter the rock (16:18). Distinct from Petros, the name.

payoffs.note: 'great is your faith' — the Canaanite woman
apistia, not-trusting: the negative of the thread, at his own hometown

threads.note: The centurion's pistis (8:10, 'not even in Israel') vs. the disciples' oligopistoi (see little-faith). Runs through the healings to 15:28 and the mountain-moving sayings.

payoffs.note: the disciples handed over — to councils, in floggings, by their own families
'all things were handed over to me by my Father' — the one bright, non-betraying use of paradidōmi in the whole gospel
'the Son of Man is about to be handed over' — the verb turns toward the passion

threads.note: paradidōmi — Judas is introduced by it at 10:4, then it fires three times for the disciples (10:17, 19, 21); from 17:22 on it becomes the governing verb of the passion.

payoffs.note: 'take up his cross and follow me' — restated right at the apo tote hinge
the literal cross — Simon carries it, the mockers name it

threads.note: stauros — first at 10:38 as a general condition of following, well before any passion prediction; recurs at 16:24 and then the crucifixion itself.

payoffs.note: one able to destroy body and life; finding/losing one's life; a wage that cannot be lost
'the lost sheep of the house of Israel' again
the one lost sheep left for — the shepherd goes after it
the Pharisees plot 'how they might destroy him' — the verb of Herod's plot against the child (2:13).

threads.note: apollymi — the lost sheep (10:6), then the losing that is done on purpose (10:39) and a reward never lost (10:42); the lost sheep returns at 15:24 and 18:12-14.

payoffs.note: four imperatives against fear in six verses — the discourse's spine
'take courage — do not be afraid' (mē phobeisthe), verbatim, on the sea
the disciples terrified at the transfiguration; 'do not be afraid'
'I was afraid' — the one-talent servant's account of himself
the centurion and the guard terrified at the earthquake
the guards shake for fear; 'do not be afraid' to the women, twice
‘do not fear’ at the sea, between the mission charge (10:26–31) and the empty tomb (28:5, 10)

threads.note: phobeō — the mē phobeisthe imperative saturates 10:26-31 and then recurs verbatim at the two most loaded moments, the sea (14:27) and the empty tomb (28:5, 10).

threads.gloss: trip up / trap-trigger, cause to stumble

payoffs.note: 'blessed is whoever isn't tripped up by me' — the little beatitude
every disciple is tripped up over Jesus in one night
The shallow hearer is 'immediately tripped up' under pressure (13:21); at the harvest the trip-traps themselves are collected out of the kingdom (13:41).
Nazareth is ‘tripped up in him’ — the very thing 11:6 called a person blessed for avoiding

threads.note: skandalizō — the eye/hand that trips you up (5:29-30) is the thread's true open; the little beatitude of 11:6 warns John gently, then 26:31-33 pays it off catastrophically.

payoffs.note: Jesus repeats John's proclamation verbatim at the apo-tote hinge
the towns that saw the most and turned the least — the summons comes back as a verdict
Nineveh turned at Jonah's proclamation; the Galilean towns did not (11:20–21).

threads.note: metanoeite — John's proclamation (3:2), repeated on Jesus' own lips (4:17), returns as an indictment on the unrepentant towns (11:20).

payoffs.note: the generation of 11:16 now named 'evil and adulterous,' judged by Ninevites and a southern queen.

threads.note: genea shifts from the literal genealogical generations of 1:17 to a moral class of people, opening its tracked sense at 11:16 ('this generation'). The 1:17 occurrence is tagged for lexical completeness, not claimed as the same sense.

payoffs.note: the same call that gathered the four at the sea now gathers the weary

threads.note: deute — 'come here, and I will make you fishers of men' (4:19) is the thread's true open; the invitation returns at 11:28 to all who labor.

payoffs.note: the beatitude's promise becomes Jesus' own self-description

threads.note: praeis — 'blessed are the gentle' (5:5) is the thread's true open; Jesus claims the word of himself at 11:29.

threads.gloss: be well pleased, take delight in

payoffs.note: the Father's spoken delight at the baptism recurs in Jesus' own prayer
Isaiah 42 in the words of the baptism voice (3:17) — 'my beloved, in whom I delighted' — and again at 17:5.

threads.note: eudokēsa — the Father's voice at the baptism (3:17) is the thread's true open; the same word recurs in Jesus' prayer at 11:26.

threads.gloss: raise up, rouse from lying down

payoffs.note: the first healing-as-raising
the ruler's daughter raised
must be raised on the third day — the verb turns toward the resurrection
he is raised, just as he said
the gospel’s first ‘raised from the dead’ comes from John’s killer, and is misapplied

threads.note: egeirō spans the mundane (get up, rouse from sleep, 1:24) and the resurrection sense it grows into. Every occurrence tagged; the trajectory is 1:24 -> the healings -> 16:21 -> the empty tomb.

payoffs.note: peace given or withheld at the threshold, then 'I didn't come to bring peace but a sword'

threads.note: 'Blessed are the peacemakers' (5:9) sets up the mission discourse's harder word: the peace a household may not deserve, and the sword Jesus says he brings instead (10:34).

payoffs.note: 'good news is proclaimed to the poor' — the answer to John's question

threads.note: euangelion — the summary refrain of 4:23/9:35 becomes John's own answer at 11:5, then a global horizon (24:14) and the woman's memorial (26:13).

payoffs.note: the reward already paid in full — showy piety's wage is the applause it got
a prophet's wage, a righteous person's wage, a cup of water's wage

threads.note: misthos — 'great is your wage in the skies' (5:12) sets the terms the Sermon keeps returning to: a wage that can be spent early (6:1-16) or never lost (10:42).

payoffs.note: 'Our Father' — the prayer itself
the mutual knowing of Father and Son
'The kingdom of their Father' — the only time Matthew says 'their' Father's kingdom.

threads.note: patēr — tagged at every occurrence including the ordinary human sense (2:22, Herod's father); the tracked thread proper opens at 5:16, 'your Father who is in the skies,' Matthew's characteristic address for God.

payoffs.note: 'fulfill all righteousness' — at the baptism
by your words you will be shown to be in the right — the verdict turned onto the accusers' own speech.
'The righteous will blaze out like the sun' — Daniel 12:3's resurrection light; separated 'from the midst' at 13:49.

threads.note: dikaios / dikaiosynē — Joseph 'a righteous man' (1:19) opens it; the Sermon makes righteousness the thing hungered for, persecuted for, and exceeded (5:6-20), then sought first (6:33).

payoffs.note: 'seek first the kingdom' — reversing Herod's seeking
'seek, and you will find'
The Sermon's 'seek first the kingdom' (6:33) and 'seek and y'all will find' (7:7) acted out: the merchant seeks, finds, sells all.

threads.note: zēteō — Herod seeks the child to destroy him (2:13); the Sermon turns the same verb toward the kingdom (6:33) and toward prayer itself (7:7).

payoffs.note: the Spirit descending at the baptism
'poor in spirit'

threads.note: pneuma — conceived of the Holy Spirit (1:18) to the Spirit descending like a dove (3:16) to the Sermon's first beatitude (5:3) to the unforgivable sin against the Spirit (12:31-32).

payoffs.note: Jesus repeats John's proclamation verbatim at the apo-tote hinge
the kingdom parables
'the kingdom of God has arrived upon y'all' — no longer only drawn near (3:2, 4:17), but arrived.

threads.note: basileia — 'the kingdom of the skies has drawn near' (3:2, 4:17) governs the Sermon's beatitudes and the parables to come. Distinct from basileus 'king' (10:18, 17:25, 18:23, 22:2), a different word not tracked here.

payoffs.note: evil people who still know how to give good gifts; the tree known by its fruit
the evil one snatches the seed; the sons of the evil one

threads.note: ponēros — tagged from its first occurrence (5:11) but the tracked thread proper opens at the Lord's Prayer's 'deliver us from the evil one' (6:13), which the Sermon and the parables keep answering.

payoffs.note: fear the one who can destroy both soul and body in Gehenna

threads.note: geenna — the Hinnom Valley's name for judgment, first at 5:22 (the Sermon's escalating anger-warnings), returning at 10:28 and the woes of 23.
peirazō — 'the tester' approaches in the wilderness (4:3); the same verb returns whenever the Pharisees try to trap Jesus.

payoffs.note: 'fulfill all righteousness'
'not to abolish but to fulfill'
the longest formula quotation in Matthew: Isaiah's servant who will not quarrel.
The prophet's word is 'filled full' (13:35); thirteen verses later the dragnet is 'filled full' (13:48).

threads.note: plēroō — the formula-quotation verb (1:22 and on) becomes Jesus' own stated relationship to the Law and the Prophets (5:17).

payoffs.note: the same verb the devil demands and the Deuteronomy reply refuses him
the learners’ first bowing before him, after 4:10 reserved worship for God alone

threads.note: proskyneō — the magi's worship (2:2, 2:11) is what the devil demands for himself (4:9) and Jesus refuses him with Deut 6:13; the risen Jesus receives it again at 28:9, 17.

payoffs.note: 'I didn't come to call the righteous but sinners'
the wedding banquet's invited guests
'do not be called rabbi'

threads.note: kaleō — the naming at 1:21 ('you shall call his name Jesus') becomes the calling of the unworthy (9:13) and the vocabulary of the kingdom's invitations. Distinct from prefixed compounds (parakaleō 'urge', proskaleomai 'summon', ekklēsia 'assembly'), each its own word.

payoffs.note: a plot to destroy him, then withdrawal — the pattern of 2:13–14, repeated in the adult ministry.
John’s death, like his arrest at 4:12, sends Jesus out of Herod’s reach

threads.note: anachōreō — the magi withdraw by another road (2:12); Joseph withdraws to Egypt then Nazareth (2:13-22); Jesus withdraws at news of John's arrest (4:12) and before the ruler's daughter is raised (9:24).
axios — fruit worthy of repentance (3:8) becomes the mission discourse's repeated test of who and what is worthy (10:10-38).

payoffs.note: the verb 'follow' finally lands cleanly on the learners themselves
John's learners vs. Jesus' learners — the fasting question turns on the label
John, in prison, sends through his own learners to ask
Jesus stretches out his hand over his learners: 'look — my mother and my brothers.'
'Every scribe made a learner' — first use of mathēteuō, the verb of the final commission (28:19).
John’s own learners bury him and come to Jesus, as they did at 11:2

threads.note: mathētēs — 'learner,' from manthanō, 'to learn.' Rendered 'learner' rather than the loan-word 'disciple' throughout the running translation, to keep the ordinary sense of the word audible.

payoffs.note: the very acts of power just paraded as 7:22's empty boast are now Galilee's own unrepented evidence
few acts of power at home, for lack of trust — and Herod credits the acts of power to a dead John (14:2)

threads.note: dynamis — 'act of power, mighty work.' Kept literal rather than 'miracle' (which implies a modern category of the supernatural Matthew doesn't use) or 'power' alone (which loses the countable, event-shaped sense — these are things done, plural).

payoffs.note: John's own title, Immerser, recurs as the mission he began is assessed

threads.note: Promoted from unit-03's local palette when the noun baptistēs ('Immerser') recurred as John's title at 11:11-12. Rendered 'immerse / Immerser' throughout — never 'baptize / Baptist' — to keep the ordinary washing-verb sense audible.

payoffs.note: the same verb Jesus used of food and clothing now covers what to say under arrest
The Sermon's forbidden care (6:25–34) returns as a thorn: 'the care that pulls apart, of the age' chokes the word of the kingdom.

threads.note: Promoted from unit-06's local palette when merimnaō recurred at 10:19. Related to merizō, 'to divide' — kept as the clumsier 'pulled apart with care' rather than smoother 'worry' or 'anxious,' to keep the division-sense visible.

payoffs.note: cleansing the leprous becomes one of the four powers handed to the Twelve

threads.note: Promoted from unit-08's local palette when katharizō recurred in the mission charge at 10:8.

payoffs.note: 'do not judge' — the verdict you give is the one you get
the day of judgment enters the mission charge
the day of judgment weighed against the Galilean towns
the servant announces judgment to the nations; Ninevites and the southern queen will rise in the judgment and judge against this generation

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): a unit-07 local root that recurred through 10:15, 11:22–24 and all of 12. krinō · krisis · kritēs · katakrinō; 5:40 krithēnai is rendered 'sue' (go to law).

payoffs.note: 'by their fruits y'all will know them'
the tree known by its fruit, turned on the accusers
The good earth 'kept giving fruit' — a hundred, sixty, thirty; the thorny soil ends 'fruitless' (13:22).

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): unit-07 local root recurring at 12:33.

payoffs.note: treasure on earth vs. in the skies
the good person brings good out of a good treasure

The treasure y'all were told to store in the skies (6:19–21) is found hidden in a field, and a man sells all he has for it; cf. Prov 2:4, wisdom sought 'as hidden treasures.' At 13:52 the scribe-learner throws out of his treasure-store new and old (cf. 12:35).

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20): unit-06 local root recurring at 12:35.
Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The sign of Jonah; returns at 16:1–4, 24:3, 24:24, 24:30 and Judas's sign (26:48).

payoffs.note: the charge laid against Jesus (9:3) turned back on his accusers: the defaming of the Spirit

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). Rendered 'defame' (not the loan-word 'blaspheme'; not 'slander', which is kept for diabolos). 9:3 changed from 'blasphemes' to match. Ahead: 15:19, 26:65, 27:39.

payoffs.note: the house on rock and the house on sand
'the lost sheep of the house of Israel'
the divided house, the strong man's house, the swept house the spirit returns to
Jesus goes out of the house to the crowds (13:1) and back in with the learners alone (13:36) — the inside/outside line of 12:46–50 acted out.

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). oikia · oikos and oikiakos ('household'); oikodespotēs ('master of the house') is not tagged. Ahead: 'y'all's house is left desolate' (23:38).

payoffs.note: John’s ‘it is not permitted for you to have her’ turns the legal-question verb on the king himself

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The legal-question verb; every Matthean use is a dispute over what Torah allows (14:4, 19:3, 20:15, 22:17, 27:6).
Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). The leaders 'take counsel' — 12:14, 22:15, 27:1, 27:7, 28:12: the plot from the Sabbath healing to the bribed guards.

payoffs.note: the rest the unclean spirit seeks and cannot find

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-12 port (2026-09-20). Ahead: 'sleep on and take rest' (26:45).

payoffs.note: Wheat and weeds grow together until the harvest; the reapers are told to gather the weeds first.
'The harvest is the completion of an age, and the reapers are angels.'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): a unit-10 local root that recurred at 13:30, 39. therismos · theristēs · therizō. Ahead: reaping where you did not sow (25:24, 26).

payoffs.note: the speck and the log in the eye
eyes closed by the people; 'blessed are y'all's eyes, because they see'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): a unit-07 local root recurring at 13:15–16. ophthalmos, every form.

payoffs.note: things hidden from the wise and revealed to infants
yeast hidden in flour, things hidden since the world's foundation, treasure hidden in a field

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): kryptō and compounds; a unit-11 local root that recurred at 13:33, 35, 44. Ahead: the talent hidden in the ground (25:18, 25).

payoffs.note: gentle and lowly in heart
the mouth speaks from the overflow of the heart
'this people's heart has grown thick'; the word sown 'in his heart' is snatched

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): kardia, every form. Ahead: 15:8–19 (heart vs lips; what defiles) and 22:37 (the Shema).

payoffs.note: the seed among the thorns is choked by care and the deceit of wealth

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): akantha; few occurrences, all placed. Gen 3:18 echo. Ahead: the crown of thorns (27:29).

payoffs.note: a person's enemies will be those of his own household
an enemy sowed the weeds; 'the enemy who sowed them is the slanderer'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): echthros / echthra. Ahead: 22:44.

payoffs.note: the shallow hearer receives the word with joy; the finder of treasure goes 'from his joy' and sells all

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): chara and chairō ('rejoice'; also the 'Hail!' greetings at 26:49, 27:29). Rootless joy (13:20) against joy that sells everything (13:44). Ahead: 25:21, 23 and 28:8.

payoffs.note: seeing they do not see, hearing they do not understand; the good soil 'understands'; 'Did y'all understand all these things? They say to him, Yes.'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): syniēmi. Matthew credits the learners with it where Mark stresses their confusion. Ahead: 15:10; 16:12; 17:13.

payoffs.note: the birds do not gather into barns
the one not gathering with me scatters
the crowds gather; gather the wheat into my barn; the dragnet gathers of every kind

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): synagō · episynagō; synagōgē (synagogue) is a separate word and not tagged. John's harvest (3:12) is reframed as delayed at 13:30. Ahead: 22:10–34; 24:28, 31; 25:24–26.

payoffs.note: one cannot plunder the strong man's house unless he first binds him
the evil one comes and snatches what was sown in his heart

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): harpazō and compounds (diarpazō); harpax ('ravenous', 7:15) deliberately left untagged. A tight three-unit arc: the kingdom snatched, the strong man plundered, the seed snatched back.

payoffs.note: a rotten tree makes rotten fruit
they gather the good into vessels; the rotten they throw outside

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): sapros. Rotten tree and worthless catch share one verdict word.

payoffs.note: 'so it will be in the completion of the age'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): fixed phrase synteleia tou aiōnos. Opens in a harvest parable, closes as the horizon of the Emmanuel promise. Ahead: 24:3; 28:20.

threads.translit: ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn
threads.gloss: "the weeping and the grinding of the teeth"

payoffs.note: 'there will be the weeping and the grinding of the teeth'

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): fixed phrase, Matthew's signature refrain. Ahead: 22:13; 24:51; 25:30.

payoffs.note: the angels collect out of his kingdom all the stumbling-blocks and those doing lawlessness

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): anomia. Four occurrences, all at moments of judgment. Ahead: 23:28; 24:12.

payoffs.note: the master of the house and his slaves; the scribe made a learner is like a master of a house

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-13 port (2026-09-26): oikodespotēs. The learner becomes like his master (10:25 → 13:52). The `house` thread deliberately excludes it. Ahead: 20:1, 11; 21:33; 24:43.

payoffs.note: the king was grieved: Herod’s sorrow, the first of six

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): lypeō. Herod is grieved at 14:9; the last is Jesus in Gethsemane (26:37). Ahead: 17:23, 18:31, 19:22, 26:22, 26:37.

payoffs.note: Peter: “why did you waver?”

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): distazō. Peter at 14:31 and the Eleven at 28:17, both beside worship. Ahead: 28:17.

payoffs.note: Jesus’ gut-wrenched response to the crowd that followed him to the desert place, after Herod’s feast

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): splanchnizomai. The one emotion Matthew names in Jesus repeatedly (9:36, 14:14, 15:32, 20:34); 18:27 gives it to a king. Ahead: 15:32, 18:27, 20:34.

payoffs.note: to the woman; the second of three
“Take heart, it is I; do not fear”, spoken to the boat before the rescue

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): tharseō. Always Jesus, always before a rescue (9:2, 9:22, 14:27).

payoffs.note: five breads: the wilderness refusal (4:3–4) becomes the wilderness feeding

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): artos. The wilderness refusal (4:3–4) becomes the wilderness feeding (14:17–19) and the table (26:26). Ahead: 15:26–36, 16:5–12, 26:26.

payoffs.note: Jesus withdraws to a desert place, and the crowd follows

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): erēmos, erēmia; formerly a unit-3 local root. John, the temptation, the withdrawals to a desert place. Ahead: 15:33, 23:38, 24:26.

threads.gloss: be struck out of oneself, astonished

payoffs.note: “struck out of themselves”: the astonishment of 7:28 curdles into offense

threads.note: Promoted at the unit-14 port (2026-10-01): ekplēssomai. The crowds’ astonishment at the Sermon (7:28) curdles into offense at Nazareth (13:54). Ahead: 19:25, 22:33.
